title: Metric dependence, flux sectors and constitutive geometry

items.title: Continuous differential-form integrals over smooth singular chains in Euclidean domains
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematics; no physical premises or physical claim.
items.statement:
Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $1\le k\le n$, let $\omega$ be a continuous $k$-form on $V$, and let $\sigma:\Delta^k\to V$ be a smooth singular simplex. Here a continuous $k$-form is a field of alternating covariant $k$-tensors with continuous coordinate coefficient functions; for smooth forms this is the usual type of [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. No injectivity or immersion is required. Extend pullback to this regularity by the slot formula

$$ (\sigma^*\omega)_u(v_1,\ldots,v_k):=\omega_{\sigma(u)}(D\sigma_u v_1,\ldots,D\sigma_u v_k). $$

In the fixed positive affine coordinates $u_1,\ldots,u_k$ on its standard parameter simplex, write the resulting continuous pullback as $\sigma^*\omega=g_\sigma(u)\,du_1\wedge\cdots\wedge du_k$. Define

$$\int_\sigma\omega:=\int_{\Delta^k}g_\sigma(u)\,du.$$

For a finite real smooth singular $k$-chain $c=\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma$, define $\int_c\omega:=\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\int_\sigma\omega$. The orientation is the fixed standard affine orientation; reversing a chain coefficient reverses its contribution. This definition applies to every continuous form, including forms with continuous first derivatives and their continuous exterior derivatives; $C^1$ means [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. For smooth $\omega$, this is the same affine pullback integral used in [[def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex]].

Each standard parameter simplex is compact Jordan, so every integral in the Definition exists; this is verified below.

references.title: Peter S. Park, Proof of de Rham's Theorem
references.locator: Indirect source via the actually used local def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex and def-standard-orientation-of-the-affine-simplex: smooth pullback-integral and orientation conventions. items.title: Excitation and free-current forms
items.physical_scope: Classical electromagnetism in the fixed oriented SI laboratory chart: the electromagnetic field-strength 2-form, macroscopic excitation 2-form, and free-current 3-form constructed from the existing field and material quantities. No material constitutive closure or empirical claim is included in these definitions.
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region be $U=I\times\Omega$, with nonempty open $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ and nonempty open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, in the fixed positively oriented chart $x^0=ct,x^1,x^2,x^3$. Write $dt=dx^0/c$ and $vol_3=dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. Use the framework fields $E,B,D,H$ and the free sources $\rho_f,J_f$, with their SI types, units, and regularity as defined by the existing laboratory, electromagnetic-field, and polarization/magnetization definitions. Whenever a first exterior derivative is used, the field coefficients are at least $C^1$.

Define the spatial forms

$$\mathcal E = E_1 dx^1 + E_2 dx^2 + E_3 dx^3,$$

$$\mathcal B = B_1 dx^2 \wedge dx^3 + B_2 dx^3 \wedge dx^1 + B_3 dx^1 \wedge dx^2,$$

$$\mathcal D = D_1 dx^2 \wedge dx^3 + D_2 dx^3 \wedge dx^1 + D_3 dx^1 \wedge dx^2,$$

$$\mathcal H = H_1 dx^1 + H_2 dx^2 + H_3 dx^3,$$

and

$$\mathcal J_{\mathrm{sp}} = (J_f)_1 dx^2 \wedge dx^3 + (J_f)_2 dx^3 \wedge dx^1 + (J_f)_3 dx^1 \wedge dx^2.$$

Define the spacetime field-strength, excitation, and free-current forms by

$$F = \mathcal B - dt \wedge \mathcal E,\qquad G = \mathcal D + dt \wedge \mathcal H,\qquad \mathcal J = \rho_f\,vol_3 - dt \wedge \mathcal J_{\mathrm{sp}}.$$

Thus $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ in $x^0=ct$ coordinates, consistently with the framework electromagnetic tensor. The integral of $F$ over an oriented spacetime 2-surface has units Wb; the integral of $G$ over such a surface and of $\mathcal J$ over an oriented spacetime 3-chain has units C. No relation between $G$ and the Lorentzian Hodge dual of $F$ is part of this definition; the vacuum closure is proved only in the separate vacuum branch.

For a $C^1$ $k$-form $\omega=\frac{1}{k!}\omega_{\mu_1\cdots\mu_k}dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_k}$, for $1\le k\le3$, in this fixed chart, with Greek indices in $\{0,1,2,3\}$ and repeated indices summed, define its laboratory-coordinate exterior derivative by

$$d\omega = \frac{1}{k!}\,\partial_\lambda\omega_{\mu_1\cdots\mu_k}\,dx^\lambda\wedge dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_k}.$$

When the coefficients are smooth this is the usual exterior derivative. For a continuous spatial 2-form $\beta_t$ and a finite real smooth singular 2-cycle $z=\sum_\sigma c_\sigma\sigma$ in $\Omega$, define its cycle flux at time $t$ by $\Phi_z(t)=\sum_\sigma c_\sigma\int_{\Delta^2}\sigma^*\beta_t$, using the standard affine orientation and continuous-chain integral convention of [[def-emx-continuous-chain-integral]].

items.title: Stokes identity for a C1 two-form on the standard three-simplex
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematics; no physical premises or physical claim.
items.statement:
Let $T=\{(u_1,u_2,u_3)\in\mathbb R^3:u_i\ge0,\ u_1+u_2+u_3\le1\}$ with its positive affine orientation and signed outward boundary. Let $\eta=f_1du^2\wedge du^3-f_2du^1\wedge du^3+f_3du^1\wedge du^2$ be a $C^1$ two-form on an open neighbourhood of $T$, and define

$$d\eta=(\partial_1f_1+\partial_2f_2+\partial_3f_3)du^1\wedge du^2\wedge du^3.$$

Using the continuous-form chain integral of [[def-emx-continuous-chain-integral]],

$$\int_T d\eta=\int_{\partial T}\eta.$$

items.title: Metric-free Maxwell equations and metric-dependent vacuum closure
items.physical_scope: Conditional smooth classical Maxwell model on the fixed oriented SI laboratory chart. The exterior equations encode the macroscopic component equations for C^1 fields and C^2 polarization and magnetization; the Hodge-star closure is only the stated vacuum case. Charge conservation is derived classically with the additional C^2 field regularity stated, and magnetic-flux constancy applies to a fixed lab-space cycle. No propagation or empirical claim is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty open time interval and $\Omega$ a nonempty open spatial region in the fixed oriented SI laboratory chart. Suppose $E$ and $B$ are jointly $C^1$, $P$ and $M$ are jointly $C^2$, and the fields satisfy the adopted smooth vacuum Maxwell equations. Define $D,H,\rho_f,J_f,F,G$, and the free-current form $\mathcal J$ by the framework material definitions and the excitation-form definition. Then $dF=0$ and $dG=\mathcal J$ are equivalent to the four macroscopic component equations

$$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{div}D=\rho_f,\qquad \operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD.$$

These four equations follow from the adopted smooth vacuum equations and the free/bound source definitions, without assuming a material constitutive law. On a vacuum region, where $P=M=0$, the metric-dependent closure is $G=(\mu_0 c)^{-1}\star_\eta F$, with $\star_\eta^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on 2-forms. If $E,B,P,M$ are $C^2$, then $d\mathcal J=0$, equivalently $\partial_t\rho_f+\operatorname{div}J_f=0$. For any fixed finite real smooth singular 2-cycle $z$ in $\Omega$, the magnetic flux $\Phi_z(t)$, defined by the $C^1$ cycle-integral convention of the excitation-form definition, is independent of $t\in I$ when $z$ is transported only by the laboratory-time slices.

items.title: Vacuum duality and its domain
items.physical_scope: Smooth source-free vacuum Maxwell fields in the fixed flat oriented SI laboratory chart, with the Lorentzian Hodge star of signature (-+++). The duality does not assert invariance of a material constitutive law or a boundary condition, and does not introduce magnetic charge.
items.statement:
On a region of the fixed oriented Minkowski laboratory chart with $P=M=0$ and free-current form $\mathcal J=0$, let $F$ be a $C^1$ electromagnetic field-strength 2-form and let $\theta$ be a constant real number. Then

$$F_\theta = \cos(\theta)F + \sin(\theta)\star_\eta F$$

again satisfies $dF_\theta=0$ and $d\star_\eta F_\theta=0$. This is a symmetry of the source-free vacuum equations only. With nonzero free-current form $\mathcal J$, a rotation with $\sin(\theta)\ne0$ generally fails the same no-magnetic-source equation; no duality invariance is asserted for a material closure or boundary condition without a separate compatibility proof. The companion conductor example gives a concrete boundary failure. No magnetic charge sector is adopted.

title: Metric dependence, flux sectors and constitutive geometry — Examples

items.title: Excluded interior flux is not a global source law
items.physical_scope: An ideal source-free vacuum Maxwell field on the punctured spatial region R^3 minus the origin with a specified nonzero flux parameter. The example gives no full-space magnetic-charge law, no empirical observation, and no smooth source-free extension through the excluded point.
items.statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty open time interval and $\Omega=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ in the fixed SI laboratory chart. Fix a nonzero flux parameter $\Phi$ with units Wb and a length $a=1\,\mathrm m$. Put $r=(x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2)^{1/2}$ and define the smooth static fields $E=0$ and $B=(\Phi/(4\pi))(x_1,x_2,x_3)/r^3$ on $I\times\Omega$. Set $P=M=0$ and total charge and current densities $\rho=0$ and $J=0$ there. Let $T$ be the tetrahedron with vertices $a(1,1,1)$, $a(1,-1,-1)$, $a(-1,1,-1)$, and $a(-1,-1,1)$. Label these vertices $v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3$ in the displayed order. For $0\le i\le3$, let $\sigma_i:\Delta^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be the affine map with ordered vertices $[v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_i,\ldots,v_3]$, and put $q_a(p)=a p/\|p\|$ for $p\ne0$. Set $z=\sum_{i=0}^3(-1)^{i+1}(q_a\circ\sigma_i)$. Then $z$ is a finite outward-oriented smooth singular 2-cycle on the sphere of radius $a$. For each $t\in I$, write $z_t$ for its image in the time slice under $x\mapsto(t,x)$. The exterior field satisfies the source-free vacuum Maxwell equations and has cycle flux $\Phi_z(t)=\int_{z_t}F=\Phi$, so its field-strength 2-form has no global potential on $I\times\Omega$. This exterior flux does not imply a magnetic charge in the full-space Maxwell model: any smooth full-space divergence-free extension agreeing on the sphere of radius $a$ would have zero flux there, a contradiction.

items.title: An ideal PEC boundary condition is not preserved by a vacuum duality quarter-turn
items.physical_scope: A smooth source-free vacuum field in a half-space with an ideal perfect-electric-conductor boundary condition imposed as model data. The calculation concerns that boundary condition only; it makes no claim about finite conductivity or measurements.
items.statement: On $\Omega=\{(x_1,x_2,x_3):x_3>0\}$, consider the constant vacuum field $E=0$ and $B=B_0(1,0,0)$, where $B_0\ne0$ has units T. Let $\Pi=\{x_3=0\}$, with unit normal $n=(0,0,1)$. The constant fields are understood with their continuous traces on $\Pi$. In this example, a perfect-electric-conductor (PEC) boundary means the ideal boundary model imposing $E_\parallel=E-(E\cdot n)n=0$ on $\Pi$; this condition is imposed as model data and no finite-conductivity claim is made. For $\theta=\pi/2$, the vacuum duality rotation $F_\theta=\star_\eta F$ has electric field $E_\theta=-cB_0(1,0,0)$, which is nonzero and parallel to $\Pi$. Thus the source-free vacuum duality rotation does not preserve this same PEC boundary condition.
